Crochet Mesh Bottle Holder — Easy Drawstring Bottle Bag 🤍🍶

A lightweight beige mesh holder for your water bottle — openwork net stitch, sturdy base, drawstring with wooden beads — perfect for gym, hiking, festivals.

I made this one on a sunny morning with linen on my table and light coming in warm — I had a clear water bottle with condensation on my table, just like in your photo with beige cord, wooden beads, and soft beige linen behind. A friend who always carries her bottle asked for a holder that wasn't heavy — "Can you make a mesh one I can throw in my bag?" So I sat with beige cotton cord, 5mm hook, wooden beads, and my own bottle sweating on the table, and crocheted a little net bag while my tea went cold. By afternoon it was holding my bottle, and I took it to the park. It was so light I forgot it was there.

Level Beginner — mesh net stitch + base + drawstring — evening make
Yarn Cotton cord 3mm — beige 80g — 5mm hook — wooden beads 4× 20mm, stitch markers, clear water bottle for sizing (500ml)
Size Holder about 7.5" tall × 3.5" wide flat (7" around stretched), fits standard 500ml bottle 8" tall × 2.8" diameter — mesh holes about 0.6" — drawstring about 20" long with beads

My yarn basket — beige cotton cord with wooden beads and bottle

For this holder I used cotton cord 3mm — soft beige 80 grams — not thin yarn but cord so it's sturdy and holds shape and doesn't stretch too much when bottle is full. I use a 5mm hook so mesh is open and airy — not tight — about 0.6" holes — and sturdy base. I also had wooden beads 4× 20mm light wood for drawstring ends, just like in your photo with two beads on each side of drawstring, and a clear water bottle with silver cap 500ml for sizing — bottle about 8" tall ×2.8" diameter.

My yarn basket — beige cotton cord yarn balls, wooden beads, crochet hooks, and clear water bottle with silver cap on beige linen table — beginning of mesh bottle holder — real photo.

I use beige cotton cord 3mm — not thin acrylic — it holds shape, doesn't stretch when bottle is full, and feels nice in hand — like in your photo with soft beige cord on linen.

How this mesh bottle holder is made — base + mesh net + drawstring

This holder is three parts — a solid base circle about 3.5" wide — then mesh net sides about 7.5" tall with open holes about 0.6" — made of chain and single crochet mesh — and drawstring with wooden beads about 20" long that goes through top edge and cinches to hold bottle. The whole holder is about 7.5" tall ×3.5" wide flat, which stretches to about 7" around when bottle inside — fits standard 500ml bottle 8" tall ×2.8" diameter — mesh stretches gently to hug bottle.

Base — solid circle — 3.5" wide

BASE — BEIGE COTTON CORD — 5MM — 3.5 INCH WIDE SOLID CIRCLE
Base — beige cotton cord, 5mm hook — solid base circle:
R1: magic ring, 6 sc — 6
R2: inc 6 — 12
R3: [sc, inc]6 — 18
R4: [sc 2, inc]6 — 24
R5: [sc 3, inc]6 — 30 — 30 sts — about 2.8" wide
R6: [sc 4, inc]6 — 36 — 36 sts — about 3.5" wide — base 3.5" wide — solid circle — sturdy base for bottle to sit on
R7: sc in back loop only 36 — creates edge ridge — base edge — 36 sts — base finished — 3.5" wide solid circle — do not cut yarn — continue directly into mesh net R8 working into this R7 edge

Base is magic ring 6→36 — 6 rounds — about 3.5" wide — solid circle — 36 sts at widest — then one round in back loop only to create edge ridge where mesh starts — base finished — 3.5" wide — do not cut yarn — continue directly from this R7 back-loop edge into R8 mesh — so base and mesh are one connected piece — sturdy for bottle to sit on — like bottom of holder in your photo with solid base connected to mesh sides.

Mesh net — openwork — 7.5" tall

MESH NET — BEIGE COTTON CORD — 5MM — 7.5 INCH TALL — OPENWORK 0.6 INCH HOLES
Mesh net — beige cotton cord, 5mm hook — openwork mesh sides — continuing from base without cutting yarn:
R8: continuing from R7 — do not cut yarn — ch 4 (counts as dc + ch1), *skip 1 st of R7 edge, dc in next st of R7, ch1* repeat around — working directly into R7 back-loop edge — 18 dc + 18 ch1 spaces — 18 mesh holes around — 36 sts of base become 18 mesh repeats because you skip every other st — join with sl st to 3rd chain of ch4 — first mesh round — holes about 0.6" — mesh now connected to base
R9-20: ch 4, *dc in ch1 space from previous round, ch1* repeat around — offset by half a stitch each round — dc goes into ch1 space, not into dc below — this offset creates diamond-shaped holes rather than straight stacked columns — 18 dc + 18 ch1 spaces each round — 12 rounds of mesh — each round about 0.6" tall — 12 rounds ×0.6" =7.2" tall — plus base 0.3" =7.5" tall total — mesh net 7.5" tall — openwork diamond net with 0.6" diamond holes — 18 holes around — diamond pattern from offset
Check after R14 — halfway — about 3.6" tall mesh — 18 diamond mesh holes around — 3.5" wide flat — 7" around stretched — fits bottle — if too tight add 2 mesh holes to 20 — if too loose dec 2 to 16
After R20 — 7.5" tall total — 7.2" mesh + 0.3" base — 18 diamond mesh holes around — openwork diamond mesh like in your photo with diamond holes about 0.6" — mesh holder sides — diamond shape from offset each round
R21: sc 36 — final solid round at top edge — sc in each dc and ch1 space — 36 sc — solid top edge for drawstring to go through — top edge finished — 36 sc — 3.5" wide flat, 7" around stretched

Mesh net is 18 dc + 18 ch1 spaces — 18 mesh holes around — each hole about 0.6" — 12 rounds of mesh offset — each round about 0.6" tall — 12 rounds ×0.6" =7.2" tall plus base 0.3" =7.5" tall total — you work R8 directly into R7 base edge without cutting yarn, so 36 base sts become 18 mesh repeats by skipping every other st — then R9-20 you offset by working dc into ch1 space from previous round rather than into dc below, which creates diamond-shaped holes rather than straight stacked columns — openwork diamond mesh like in your photo with beige cord net holding clear bottle — 3.5" wide flat, 7" around stretched when bottle inside — fits standard 500ml bottle 8" tall ×2.8" diameter — bottle top peeks out about 0.5" above mesh top edge — like in your photo where bottle top shows above holder.

Mesh net in progress — beige mesh diamond net laid flat on wooden table with cord tangled, purple handle hook, scissors, and water bottle with blue cap — real photo — mesh holes about 0.6" — 18 holes around — 7.5" tall.

Drawstring with wooden beads — 20" long

DRAWSTRING — BEIGE COTTON CORD + WOODEN BEADS — 20 INCH LONG
Drawstring — beige cotton cord, 5mm hook — with wooden beads:
Ch 80 — chain 80 — about 20" long — drawstring chain — 80 chains — 20" long
Thread wooden beads onto drawstring — 2 beads on each end — 4 beads total — 20mm wooden beads light wood — thread bead onto chain end, tie knot below bead to hold — bead about 0.8" wide — 2 beads per side
Weave drawstring through top edge R21 — through every other sc — in and out — around top — like drawstring channel — leaves two ends with beads on each side — like in your photo with drawstring with 2 beads on left and 2 beads on right — cinches to hold bottle
Drawstring 20" long with 4 wooden beads — 2 per side — each bead 0.8" — beads hold drawstring from slipping

Drawstring is ch80 — about 20" long — chain 80 — thread wooden beads onto ends — 2 beads per side — 4 beads total — 20mm wooden beads light wood 0.8" wide each — tie knot below each bead to hold — weave drawstring through top edge R21 through every other sc — in and out around top — leaves two ends with 2 beads each side — like in your photo where drawstring with wooden beads cinches top to hold bottle.

Finished mesh with drawstring and wooden beads — beige mesh bottle holder on beige linen with water bottle inside — drawstring with 2 wooden beads on each side — beads 0.8" wide — real photo — drawstring 20" long.

Assembly — finishing the bottle holder

ASSEMBLY — BASE + MESH + DRAWSTRING — FITS 500ML BOTTLE
Assembly — finishing mesh bottle holder:
1. Base — solid circle 3.5" wide — 6→36 — back loop ridge edge — base finished
2. Mesh net — 18 dc +18 ch1 spaces — 18 holes around — 12 rounds — 7.2" tall mesh +0.3" base =7.5" tall total — holes 0.6" — openwork diamond mesh — 36 sc top edge
3. Drawstring — ch80 — 20" long — 4 wooden beads 20mm — 2 per side — weave through top edge R21 every other sc
4. Put clear water bottle 500ml 8" tall ×2.8" diameter inside holder — bottle sits on base — mesh stretches to 7" around to hug bottle — bottle top peeks out 0.5" above top edge — like in your photo where clear bottle with silver cap shows above beige mesh holder
5. Cinch drawstring — pull both ends with beads — top cinches to hold bottle — beads keep drawstring from slipping — holder finished — 7.5" tall ×3.5" wide flat — fits bottle

I put clear water bottle 500ml inside holder — 8" tall ×2.8" diameter — bottle sits on solid base 3.5" wide — mesh net 7.5" tall stretches to 7" around to hug bottle — bottle top with silver cap peeks out about 0.5" above top edge — like in your photo where clear bottle with condensation shows above beige mesh holder with drawstring and wooden beads on sides. I cinch drawstring — pull both beaded ends — top cinches to hold bottle — beads 0.8" keep drawstring from slipping.

Finished — mesh bottle holder with bottle inside

And here it is — my easy mesh bottle holder — about 7.5" tall ×3.5" wide flat, 7" around stretched when bottle inside — fits standard 500ml bottle 8" tall ×2.8" diameter — base solid circle 3.5" wide — mesh net 12 rounds ×0.6" =7.2" tall plus base 0.3" =7.5" tall total — 18 mesh holes around, each hole about 0.6" diamond openwork — top edge 36 sc solid for drawstring — drawstring ch80 20" long with 4 wooden beads 20mm light wood 0.8" wide — 2 beads per side — like in your photo with beige cotton cord mesh holder holding clear water bottle with silver cap and condensation, drawstring with wooden beads on beige linen, floral border with "Small project, big joy!" and "Happy Crocheting!"

Finished — beige cotton cord mesh bottle holder — 7.5" tall ×3.5" wide flat — openwork diamond mesh with 0.6" holes — 18 holes around — drawstring with wooden beads — holding clear water bottle 500ml with silver cap — on beige linen — easy, cute, beginner friendly — perfect for gym, hiking, festivals, water bottles. 🤍🍶

When I took it to the park next morning with my bottle inside, a lady said, "Did you make that bottle holder? It's so cute and light!" I laughed and said, "I made it yesterday with cotton cord and wooden beads on my linen table." I hope you make yours on a sunny morning too — maybe with linen and light coming in — and use it for gym, hiking, festivals, or just daily water bottle.

— Sara
